subject: (EXTERNAL) Concerning parking at the future First Step House at 273 East 800 South
comment: To whom it may concern Hello, I currently own and live in a home at REDACTED. I have lived here since 2009. The proposed, future First Step House will be built a few houses down from where I live. My concern is that this will create a parking nightmare for residents who do not have driveways of their own. I live here with my wife and daughter. We have 3 cars and we don't have a driveway so we all park on the street. Some of my neighbors are in a similar situation. Sometimes I park in front of their houses and sometimes they park in front of mine. Sometimes I have to park in front of the building at 273 East 800 South (future First Step house) because there already are not enough parking spaces for us on the streets next to our own homes. This is inconvenient already but we make it work. I don't have a problem with this new building coming to our neighborhood. But I'm concerned that this building will not have sufficient parking for employees, residents, and visitors. I worry that this will create more difficult parking issues for a neighborhood that already does not have enough parking for current residents. Last weekend, a friend of mine came over to my house and parked across the street from my house on 8th South because it was the closest parking spot to my house. It would be unfortunate if this new development created a parking disaster for the residents of this area. I would appreciate it if this parking issue could be addressed further. Thank you Greg Minen

subject: THANK YOU for your support on Upper Yale Heights LHD!
comment: Dear Council members Thank you for your support tonight approving the creation of Upper Yale Heights LHD. It was a surprise to have the City Council vote early, but a delightful one indeed! We are grateful for this positive approval. There are only 3 streets of the 11 total streets on the 1800-1900 block of Yalecrest that have sufficient number of historically contributing houses to protect, and only on Yale Ave are the houses lived in by property owners. The remaining 8 streets on that block have experienced extensive demolitions with McMansion new construction replacements. Those McMansion containing 8 streets no longer have affordable houses. We are grateful and appreciate your efforts to save these more affordable historic houses for future residents. Thank you for your efforts and support -- Lynn K. Pershing, Ph.D.

subject: Re-Zoning for the first steps facility at 300 east 800 south
comment: Hello, I have been a home owner in the block adjacent to this proposed site since 2018. I have seen the impact that concentrated services for people who are struggling with homelessness and behavioral/mental health issues have had. It is not positive. I am aware of the urgent needs of this population, they circulate through our neighborhood and I truly wish there was more support for their needs. We already have the highest concentration of services of any neighborhood the State and the problems associated with substance abuse remain prolific. Please help these individuals reach more positive outcomes by DENYING the re-zone, thereby encouraging First Steps to secure an alternative site in a neighborhood better suited to provide a stable, safe community network. Thank you for your consideration with this matter. Derrek Draper

subject: Public Comment & Petition - Zoning Amendment at 273 E 800 S (April 15 Council Meeting)
comment: Dear Mayor and Salt Lake City Council Members, I'm writing as a resident of the Central City neighborhood regarding the proposed Zoning Map Amendment at approximately 273 East 800 South, scheduled for discussion at the April 15, 2025, Formal Council Meeting at 7:00 p.m. As someone who lives in and cares deeply about this neighborhood, I've been actively gathering input from fellow residents and community members about the impacts of continued zoning changes and the concentration of services in Central City. I'm submitting the attached petition form and survey results, which reflect the perspectives of people who believe in equitable development—especially when it comes to affordable housing and health services. Through this effort, we are urging the City Council to ensure that any zoning approval for this site is tied to: • Truly affordable housing for people earning below 30% AMI, • On-site health and supportive services for residents, • And a more equitable distribution of such services across all neighborhoods—not just in historically overburdened areas like Central City. These concerns are rooted in lived experience. Central City has long done its part. It's time for a broader, citywide approach that includes all communities in supporting vulnerable populations. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, Jenny Starley Central City

subject: Objection to proposed zoning project 273 E 800 S
comment: To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to respectfully express my opposition to the proposed zoning change at 273 E 800 S to allow for a four-story, high-density housing development intended for individuals earning less than 30% of the Area Median Income (AMI), many of whom will require behavioral health support and 24/7 on-site services. While I fully support the need for compassionate and affordable housing across our city, I am concerned that this particular proposal places an undue burden on the central city—an area that has long carried more than its fair share of deeply affordable, service-based housing. It is time for other neighborhoods to step up and share in this critical responsibility. Furthermore, the success of vulnerable residents depends on their placement in safe, stable, and balanced communities. Our neighborhood already struggles with high crime rates, strained infrastructure, and limited access to essential services. According to Salt Lake City's own crime data, central city neighborhoods experience some of the highest rates of property and violent crime in the city. Adding another high-needs, high-density development without addressing these foundational issues is not only unfair to existing residents—it also sets up future residents for hardship rather than success. In addition, the proposed RMF-45 zoning does not align with the existing character of our neighborhood. Approving this change would set a precedent for future high-density projects without adequate community engagement or long-term planning. Growth and housing solutions must be community-driven, thoughtfully integrated, and equitably distributed across Salt Lake City. I urge you to consider the cumulative impact of this zoning decision—not only on our neighborhood but on the individuals this project intends to serve. We all want a Salt Lake City that is inclusive and supportive, but that vision must be built through shared responsibility, balanced development, and planning that puts residents first. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, Mackenzie Jaggi Salt Lake City Resident

subject: City Council Agenda
comment: Councilman Puy: I hope all is well with you. I've appreciated your help in the past with the challenges and opportunities in our district in Salt Lake City. Today, I want to share feedback with you on some areas of concern that I understand will be addressed in an upcoming Council meeting. As you know, the planning commission approved an amendment put forward by the Mayor's office for a zoning change with more restrictions on parking in Salt Lake. This along with the "Road Diets", traffic calming, reduced street parking, higher fines and rates, and lower speed limits are choking the city. With these continued changes, it is becoming increasingly difficult to do business in Salt Lake City. With the city's multi-million dollar deficit, we should be looking for ways to increase business not raise taxes on a reduced amount of business. The restaurant tax is already at 8.75%. Other taxes have been implemented where Salt Lake City residents shouldn't an unfair share. The ongoing "road diets" add to commute times and I would suspect add to our pollution problem. Let's make Utah's Capitol City the best place to live, work, play AND do business. If we make it easier for people to do business in the City we will attract more businesses, more residents and more visitors. As a resident and business owner, I want only the best for Salt Lake City. Please do not support the Mayor's proposed zoning change. Thank you, Chris Hemmersmeier CEO Jerry Seine Dealerships

subject: SLC Public Safety Plan 2025 under performing__12
comment: To whom it may concern: It has been 3-months since the Salt Lake City Public Safety Plan was created. The suggestions the Mayor and her team created within the Public Safety Plan are not being initiated on the streets of Salt Lake City — see photos below. Additionally, the Mayor's office, the City of Salt Lake Parking enforcement Department, and the Salt Lake Police Department are not enforcing City ordinances let alone the suggestions made to Governor Cox within the 2025 Salt Lake City Public Safety Plan. This behavior would not be tolerated in the Greater Avenues neighborhood, East Central neighborhood, or the East Benches neighborhood. However, it is tolerated by the Mayor's office and the City departments the Mayor regulates on the Westside neighborhoods — alas. The Westside and its residents need the City of Salt Lake, the SLC Police Department, the City of Salt Lake Parking Enforcement Department, and the District Representatives who supposedly represent the citizens of Salt Lake to begin holding people accountable for their actions and/or inactions with violating City ordinances; all the while who continue to create Public Health and Public Safety environments. Is this the "vision" the Mayor of SLC and her team had when creating the 2025 Public Safety Plan: "The City's public spaces will be safe, clean, and welcoming to everyone."? (Pg. 7) — see photos below. Is this what is meant in the 2025 Public Safety Plan when it states: "The City Council will be presented with an updated ordinance aimed at addressing the negative impacts of camping including updates to the regulations prohibiting the use of RVs for camping on streets in the City." (Pg. 32) — see photos below. When will the regulations be enacted let alone created? When will the recommendations be allowed to be enforced by the departments the Mayor oversees? Regards, Adam Gmyrek Glendale 8

subject: Opportunity to protect Medicaid for homeless individuals
comment: Mayor and Council, As many of you know, my day job is state and federal health policy and I wanted to offer my support in the event you wanted to use your voice and connections to push back on proposed Medicaid cuts at the federal level. The clear connection is that cuts in funding or de facto cuts in funding through things like a work requirement would make it nearly impossible for individuals experiencing homelessness and getting behavioral health and/or drug use disorder treatment to maintain their coverage so they can exit the street-to-jail-to-street cycle. The easiest thing to do is to text our delegation and let them know this would hamper our efforts to promote safety in the city. I might also suggest reaching out to the donor class that have shown a particular interest on this topic (e.g. the Smith Entertainment Group, the LHM Group). Let me know if you want talking points or other resources. Happy to connect with anyone interested on this. Feel free to text me. -- Tom Merritt

subject: Panhandling sign installation - Redwood Rd & I-80 interchange.
comment: Ms. Petro-Eschler, The sign in the attached photo below was taken at the I-15 SB 3050 exit ramp to W 1300 S, SLC, UT 84115 Would it be possible to have a sign similar to the one below installed at: I-80 & Redwood Rd WB off ramp exit 118 I-215 & Redwood Rd WB off ramp exit 22 There continues to be panhandling at both off-ramps on a daily basis. As warmer weather is upon the Salt Lake Valley the panhandling will only increase. The panhandlers filter through both lanes holding signs asking for money when traffic is stopped causing a safety hazard to themselves and to the drivers waiting for the traffic light to turn green. I've observed a man in a wheelchair stationed in-between both traffic lanes holding a sign asking for money. Also, the amount of trash generated and its buildup by the panhandlers at the I-215 & Redwood Rd WB off ramp exit 22 light / intersection can be overwhelming at times, and an eyesore. More degradation of our neighborhoods in District 1 & District 2 by the homeless. The 2025 Salt Lake Public Safety Plan states: "The City's public spaces will be safe, clean, and welcoming." (Pg. 7) "The City's public spaces will be safe, clean, and inviting to all law-abiding people." (Pg. 7) "The City will be accountable for what is in our control and be clear and collaborative with partners on what resources are needed for the entire system to be successful." (pg. 7) (...(2) the City is perceived as lenient on enforcing ordinances against camping, loitering, and panhandling; and...] (pg.17) The perception is correct, especially within the Westside neighborhoods. Would you be able to speak with a supervisor at the City of Salt Lake transportation Department and facilitate the installation of signs informing drivers that it is unlawful to transfer money / property while at said intersections? As you know, public safety is paramount. I look forward to your timely response. Thank you. Regards, Adam Gmyrek

subject: Thank you for you and your team's efforts on the Jordan River Trail on the West Side!
comment: Dear Chief Redd, I'm writing to extend my sincere thanks to you and your team for the increased enforcement efforts currently underway along the Jordan River Trail on the city's west side. These efforts have not gone unnoticed. For far too long, this beautiful stretch of our city has struggled under the weight of crime and unsafe conditions. The stepped-up patrols are making a real difference, and many of us who live near and use the trail regularly are finally beginning to feel a renewed sense of safety and pride in this public space. We are encouraged by the progress and deeply grateful for your department's commitment. It's our hope that this initiative will become a permanent presence to ensure the west side is no longer an afterthought when it comes to public safety. Our community deserves the same level of protection and peace of mind as every other part of Salt Lake City. Thank you again for your leadership and for prioritizing the wellbeing of all residents. Please extend our appreciation to the officers out on the trail each day—they're making a real impact. Warm regards, Ted Dumont Kevin Reeves

subject: Voicemail to City Council
comment: I just wanted to say that I think you should help out the homeless more to where they can get in work and save their bed so that they have a secure place to sleep and be able to work around the areas of operation with the shelters. So they have more time to work and come in as they need to based on their hours at work. That is all I have to say. Thank you.

subject: homeless place to stay
comment: Respectfully, Council Members, I suggested a number of years ago (8 or 9) to the Mayor's office (and several times since) that what is needed is a "KOA" for those who do not want to be enclosed or who may be waiting for an opening in a shelter. I was originally told by the Mayor's office (each time) that it is not humane to leave them unsheltered (the official policy cannot be that the City expects them to remain unhoused). However, it is not "humane" to chase them from place to place as has been happening. I suggested the use of the old Fleet block but was told that it had contamination and could not be used. Now that it is demolished I hope it is actually being "de-contaminated". There is surely a block of land that can be fitted with lighting, water and hygiene facilities with trash removal and police oversight (just someone they can turn to for help if necessary - NOT guards as in a prison) that is more reasonable than expecting to build "tiny homes" and affordable housing. A regular place to stay with a small space for "stuff" which will also provide an address and prevent them from being CHASED all over the city. It will probably also be cheaper than spending weekly hazmat teams to clean up what is currently happening. Ellen Hardman

subject: City Budget
comment: I would like to know more about the proposed City budget. I recommend that this information be made easily accessible to all SLC residents in a format similar to the one produced by the Los Angeles City Controller Kenneth Mejia. Linked here for your review: https://budget.lacontroller.app/ I also suggest giving residents the ability to submit their own budget recommendations such as can be found here: https://mytlabudget.lacontroller.app/summarized Then I strongly suggest your data manager take the median data and present it to the Council to be read into the record during a budgeting meeting. Thank you for taking my input as a resident of SLC that wants to see a flourishing civil life in our city where all residents can play a meaningful role in shaping our community.

subject: Budget Reallocation
comment: I propose a 10–15% reduction in the SLCPD budget, with the reallocated funds directed toward mental health services, affordable housing, community-based safety programs, youth initiatives, and public infrastructure improvements. These investments will address systemic issues and promote a more equitable and supportive community.

This city is in a beautiful area of the world, and the power lines, and other utility lines need to go underground.

subject: Voicemail City Council
comment: I am a very concerned Salt Lake City resident and Salt Lake County resident. I just wanted to say that I really like living out here in Salt Lake. I have lived in other parts of the state. There is one thing that I have found that really needs our attention. Please please please add more time to the crosswalks and I mean all of them. There are people in the town who are in walkers and strollers and wheelchairs and canes. I am one of them and it is so hard for me to get across before the lights changes. I ride the bus and trax and it can be really scary. I know a person who was hit and killed. She was 85 and I am sure she couldn't get across in enough time.

subject: Voicemail to City Council
comment: I am a resident of Rose Park. I appreciate what you are doing trying to clean up that river area but we also are very concerned about our roads out here. We haven't had anything done to these roads in years. Especially the major intersections 6th North and 10th North and 8th West. Please lets get something done on these roads. These cars we buy are getting all torn up. Thank you for your time.

subject: Projects to prioritize
comment: Hello, I received the mailing from the city council inviting suggestions to prioritize in the city budget. My family and I have lived in the area north of Sugarhouse for 50 years. The roads we use every day are in such poor shape that it is almost like driving on unpaved bumpy roads in the wilderness. Specifically, 17th South between 11th East and 13th East; 13th South between 11th East and 13th East; and 13th East between 9th South and 13th South. In the 50 years I've lived here, I don't recall these areas ever having been repaved. There are other areas of poor roads as well, too many to list here. On certain roads, I can tell when I have left the boundaries of Salt Lake City, because the roads get smoother. Phil Snow
